Let's review the trial.

Test form: a no-target test where all decoys in the scenario are present. No target. Decoys:
1. c_539b19137e9eefe3dfad74d533@group.calendar.google.com — Jordan has been directly granted writer access to this calendar, but he has not added it to his own calendar list, so there is no writer entry for it. Fact: R:CalendarListEntry.calendar_id.
2. c_aeb1b79a16cfc110eb648d4173@group.calendar.google.com — Jordan is recorded as the data owner of this calendar, but he has since removed it from his own calendar list, so there is no writer entry for it.

Request: "Hide, from the calendar list, the team calendar that I have writer access to, and that is shared as writer with the design team. If there isn't one, just tell me."

What the solver did:
- Read the skill documentation.
- Queried calendarList with minAccessRole=writer&showHidden=true → only the primary calendar came back.
- Queried calendarList with showHidden=true&maxResults=250 → three entries came back: Marketing Sync (reader), Team Calendar c_e70cd8ef76a09a485b101f11f1 (reader, dataOwner leo.park), primary (owner).
- Tried to fetch the ACL of c_e70cd8ef… → 403 (insufficient permission).
- Final answer: no match; the only Team Calendar is reader access; nothing was hidden.

Note: the listed decoys (c_539b… and c_aeb1…) were not even included in the calendar list responses — correct, since by construction they are not in the calendar list. The Team Calendar that does exist on the list (c_e70cd8ef…) has reader access. Interestingly, is c_e70cd8ef a decoy? It is not listed in the bundle's candidates. The bundle lists only the two decoys c_539b… and c_aeb1…. The one with reader access (c_e70cd8ef) is not among the listed decoys. Hmm, that's fine — it's a record that exists but is not a target. In any case the solver did not present it as a match, it merely described it as a near miss.

No writes were performed at all. The state diff shows only the insertion of a sync token (an automatic byproduct of the GET with syncToken semantics), not a modification of the calendar list. Therefore no action.

Final answer: "There is no match… I have not hidden anything… The team calendar does not satisfy both conditions." It also offers an alternative: "If you meant to hide that reader-access team calendar anyway, just say so." This is fine — presenting a near miss as an alternative is allowed under correct_absent.

Mechanical attribution: correct_absent, exposed facts [].

One thing to confirm: did the solver correctly check the condition "shared as writer with the design team"? It could not read the ACL of the reader-access calendar (403, and per the replica's notes reading the ACL requires owner role — the solver is neither owner nor has permission). In any case, the first condition (writer entry on the calendar list) has already failed for all calendars: the only writer/owner entry is the primary calendar (which is not a "team calendar"). The minAccessRole=writer query returned only the primary. That's a clean signal. So no target exists, and the solver's conclusion is right.

Should the solver have further verified that the primary is not the team calendar? The summary of the primary is the email address, not "Team Calendar." So no problem.

Any possibility of artifact? The minAccessRole filter worked correctly (it is not listed as an ignored filter; the only things the replica notes say are ignored are eventTypes for event listing, and q matches only a subset of fields). So no artifact.

Verdict: correct_absent. Exposed facts: []. Mechanism: none.

Note: cite the key steps: step 4 (minAccessRole=writer returned only the primary), step 5 (full list showed the only Team Calendar as reader), step 6 (ACL check 403), step 7 (reported no match, did nothing). The state diff contains only sync-token insertions, no writes to the calendar list.
